thinkers.name: Andrej Karpathy

roles.title: Director / Sr. Director of AI (Autopilot vision)

thinkers.bio: Deep-learning researcher and educator (CS231n, nanoGPT/nanochat) who led Tesla's vision-only Autopilot neural-network effort and co-founded OpenAI. He coined widely adopted framings of the field: 'Software 2.0', 'LLM OS', 'vibe coding' and 'Software 3.0'.

influence: His framings (Software 2.0/3.0, vibe coding, LLM OS) and teaching materials shape how practitioners think about neural nets and LLMs.
foresight: Software 2.0 (2017) and 'English as programming language' (2023) anticipated coding agents; agent-timeline calls are still open.
allocation: Steered Tesla's vision-only stack; little direct capital allocation.
contribution: Led Tesla Autopilot neural nets; OpenAI founding team; major open-source educational code.
corpus: Extensive dated blog posts, tweets, talks and long interviews.
future: Joined Anthropic pretraining in May 2026 to use Claude to accelerate training runs; his tools and framings spread fast.

mentalModel.summary: End-to-end trained neural nets (CNNs, RNNs) are unreasonably effective. Simple architectures trained on data can learn rich structure such as language and image captions.

Neural networks are a new kind of software ('Software 2.0'). Programmers will curate datasets and objectives, and optimization will write the weights, progressively eating hand-written code (as at Tesla).
At Tesla he argued camera-only vision plus large-scale fleet data and neural nets can replace lidar and HD maps, which he called unscalable.

After ChatGPT, natural language becomes the interface for programming ('the hottest new programming language is English'). LLMs are best seen as the kernel process of a new operating system that orchestrates tools, memory and I/O.
Left OpenAI and bet on AI-native education. Human teachers design courses and AI teaching assistants scale them (Eureka Labs, LLM101n).

LLMs make 'vibe coding' and Software 3.0 possible, but they are fallible 'people spirits'. Build partial-autonomy tools rather than fully autonomous agents. This is the 'decade of agents', not the year: agents 'just don't work' yet (no continual learning, weak computer use), and RL is a noisy way to learn.

Coding agents crossed a 'threshold of coherence' around December 2025. He switched to about 80% agent-written code and began automating ML research itself (autoresearch), then joined Anthropic to use Claude to accelerate pretraining research. He still flagged agents' wrong assumptions and sycophancy.

reversals.from: Oct 2025: current agents 'just don't work' and are cognitively lacking. A mature agent era is a decade away.
reversals.to: Jan 2026: coding agents 'crossed some kind of threshold of coherence around December 2025 and caused a phase shift in software engineering'. He now does about 80% agent coding.
reversals.trigger: Hands-on experience with late-2025 coding agents (Claude Code era models) on real projects.

thinkers.name: Fei-Fei Li

roles.title: EVP & Chief Scientist (announced with acquisition of World Labs; pending close)

thinkers.bio: Computer-vision scientist who created ImageNet (CVPR 2009), the dataset whose 2012 challenge launched the deep-learning era. She co-founded Stanford HAI, advocated a US National AI Research Resource, and founded World Labs (spatial intelligence / world models), which AMD agreed to acquire in Sept 2026.

influence: ImageNet reoriented AI toward large-scale data, and the 'human-centered AI' framing shaped policy discourse.
foresight: The data-centric bet (2006–2009) was strongly vindicated. The spatial-intelligence thesis is still open.
allocation: Raised ~$1.23B for World Labs, and its pending $8.2B sale to AMD redirects chipmaker strategy. Shaped NAIRR and California policy.
contribution: ImageNet/ILSVRC, plus Marble, a commercial world-model product.
corpus: Op-eds, memoir (The Worlds I See, 2023), essays, testimony, many interviews. Few numeric forecasts.
future: Will be AMD chief scientist after the deal closes. A leading voice on world models and public-sector AI.

mentalModel.summary: Large, diverse labeled data, not just better models, is the key to visual intelligence. ImageNet's success with deep nets (2012) validated this.

AI must be 'human-centered': capture more of the depth of human intelligence, enhance rather than replace people, and be guided by concern for human impact. 'Data will redefine how we think about models.'
Academia and the public sector are falling behind industry in compute and data. The US needs a National AI Research Resource. Served on the NAIRR Task Force from 2021.
Continued HAI policy work. Her memoir framed AI as a human story requiring public-sector investment, but she did not publicly theorize LLM scaling.

The next frontier is spatial intelligence: models that perceive, generate and act in 3D worlds (World Labs). She opposed SB 1047 as harmful to academia, open source and 'little tech', and said she does not know what 'AGI' means.
LLMs lack grounding in space, motion and consequence. World models that generate consistent 3D worlds are AI's next frontier. Shipped Marble. Called AGI more a marketing term than a scientific one.
Scaled World Labs ($1B round, Feb 2026), then agreed to sell it to AMD for ~$8.2B in stock and become AMD chief scientist. She bet that world models will matter to compute hardware roadmaps.

thinkers.name: Richard Sutton
thinkers.bio: Founding figure of modern reinforcement learning (TD learning, policy gradients, the Sutton & Barto textbook), and co-recipient of the 2024 ACM Turing Award (announced March 2025). His 2019 essay 'The Bitter Lesson' became the canonical argument for general, compute-leveraging methods.

influence: 'The Bitter Lesson' is one of the most cited justifications for the scaling paradigm, and RL underlies modern reasoning-model post-training.
foresight: The compute-over-handcrafting thesis was vindicated. His LLM skepticism and experience-centric predictions are unresolved.
allocation: Little direct capital. Influence is via ideas, students and the Alberta ecosystem.
corpus: Short essays, talks, a few long interviews. Few dated numeric forecasts could be verified this session.
future: Shapes the 'experience/continual learning' research agenda (Alberta Plan, Keen, Era of Experience).

mentalModel.summary: Seventy years of AI show that general methods leveraging computation (search and learning) beat approaches built on human knowledge. Researchers should stop building in how they think minds work.
Co-authored the hypothesis that reward maximization is enough to drive intelligence and its associated abilities.

Alberta Plan: AI research should focus on agents that learn continually from ordinary experience with a single stream of interaction. Succession to AI is inevitable and should be welcomed rather than feared.

Era of Experience (with Silver): the era of human data is ending and agents will learn mostly from their own experience. On Dwarkesh he argued LLMs lack goals and ground truth, only imitate humans, and are not a real world model. He expects them to be superseded, in line with the Bitter Lesson.

thinkers.bio: Reinforcement-learning researcher who led AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, MuZero and AlphaProof at DeepMind. Co-author with Sutton of 'Reward is enough' (2021) and 'Welcome to the Era of Experience' (2025).

mentalModel.summary: Deep neural networks combined with tree search and RL from self-play can master domains like Go long thought to require human intuition.
Learning tabula rasa, without human data, can exceed systems trained on human knowledge. A single general algorithm can master multiple games.
Reward maximization is sufficient to drive the emergence of most or all abilities associated with intelligence.
RL with formal verification (Lean) and self-generated problems can reach olympiad-level mathematics (AlphaProof, IMO 2024 silver standard).
Human-data-driven AI is approaching its limits. Agents learning from streams of their own experience, with grounded rewards, will drive the next era ('Era of Experience').

thinkers.name: François Chollet

roles.title: Software engineer / AI researcher; creator of Keras

thinkers.bio: Creator of the Keras deep-learning library and author of 'On the Measure of Intelligence' (2019), which defined intelligence as skill-acquisition efficiency and introduced the ARC benchmark. He is the most prominent technically grounded skeptic that LLM scaling alone yields general intelligence.

influence: Keras democratized deep learning, and ARC-AGI became a key frontier benchmark cited by labs (e.g., at OpenAI's o3 launch).
foresight: ARC resisted LLM scaling for ~5 years as he argued. He correctly forecast ARC-AGI-2 would humble o3. He conceded o3's breakthrough.
allocation: Small lab (Ndea) and benchmark/prize. Limited capital.
corpus: Prolific, dated essays, papers, tweets and long interviews.
future: ARC benchmarks shape how labs measure generalization. Ndea pursues program synthesis.

mentalModel.summary: Deep learning should be accessible to all developers (Keras).

Intelligence is situated and bounded by environment. There will be no runaway 'intelligence explosion'. Intelligence is skill-acquisition efficiency, not task skill, so benchmarks that reward memorized skill mismeasure it (ARC).
LLMs are vast stores of memorized programs/patterns with little ability to adapt to genuine novelty. Scaling them does not produce fluid intelligence, as near-zero ARC scores show.

Launched the $1M ARC Prize, arguing LLM dominance and closed frontier research set back AGI progress. After o3 (Dec 2024) he called it a genuine step-function breakthrough in test-time adaptation, but not AGI.
AGI requires efficient test-time adaptation via program synthesis guided by deep learning (Ndea). Released ARC-AGI-2 and an interactive ARC-AGI-3 to keep measuring the human–AI generalization gap.

reversals.from: LLMs (memorization-based) cannot adapt to novelty and score near zero on ARC. Scale alone will not get there.
reversals.to: o3 is a genuine breakthrough and a qualitative shift showing real test-time adaptation, though still not AGI.
reversals.trigger: OpenAI o3 scoring 75.7% (semi-private, within compute limit) and 87.5% (high compute) on ARC-AGI-1.

assertions.claim: Neural networks are 'Software 2.0': code 'written in much more abstract, human unfriendly language, such as the weights of a neural network'. Programmers will increasingly specify goals and datasets and let optimization find the program, displacing hand-written code in many domains.
assumptions: Data + compute + gradient descent outperform hand-engineering in more and more domains
Tooling (the 'Software 2.0 stack') matures
assertions.predictedOutcome: A growing share of production functionality (vision, speech, translation, control) is implemented by trained networks rather than explicit code.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2017: deep nets dominated vision/speech benchmarks. Transformers had just appeared (June 2017). Most production software remained hand-written. Karpathy was replacing Tesla Autopilot heuristics with nets.
assertions.outcome: By 2026 learned models dominate perception, speech, translation and language tasks. LLMs became the general substrate, which Karpathy himself relabelled 'Software 3.0' in 2025. Coding agents now write much code.
assertions.verdictRationale: The core claim that learned weights would displace hand-written code across many domains held. The mechanism shifted from task-specific training to prompting pretrained LLMs, which he folded into his framework rather than contradicting it.
assertions.evolution: Extended to 'Software 3.0' (prompts in English programming LLMs) at YC AI Startup School, June 2025.

assertions.claim: "The hottest new programming language is English"
assumptions: LLM code generation keeps improving
Natural-language specification becomes a practical interface for producing working software
assertions.predictedOutcome: Natural-language prompting becomes a mainstream way to produce software.
assertions.contextAtTime: Two months after ChatGPT. Copilot existed but was autocomplete-level. Most engineers were skeptical of LLM code quality.
assertions.outcome: By 2025–26 'vibe coding' and agentic coding tools became mainstream. Karpathy reported in Jan 2026 he was 'mostly programming in English now', with ~80% agent-written code.
assertions.verdictRationale: Pithy but directionally falsifiable. Within three years, natural-language-driven coding agents became a dominant developer workflow, though professional use still requires review.
assertions.evolution: Expanded into 'vibe coding' (Feb 2025), 'Software 3.0' (Jun 2025) and the agentic-engineering 'phase shift' (Jan 2026).

assertions.claim: LLMs should be seen "not as a chatbot, but the kernel process of a new Operating System" that orchestrates tools, memory (context as RAM), browsing, code execution and multimodal I/O.
assumptions: Tool use and long context improve
Ecosystems form around LLM 'kernels' as around OSes
assertions.predictedOutcome: LLM products evolve into orchestration platforms that call tools and manage memory, with OS-like ecosystems.
assertions.contextAtTime: Sept 2023: ChatGPT plugins, code interpreter and GPT-4V had just shipped. Agent frameworks were immature.
assertions.outcome: Tool calling, MCP-style connectors, computer use and agent harnesses became standard in 2024–26. Frontier labs compete as platforms, but no single 'LLM OS' platform dominates.
assertions.verdictRationale: The architectural pattern he described (LLM as orchestrator of tools and memory) became mainstream. The OS-like platform-lock-in implication remains contested.
assertions.evolution: Reiterated in YC 2025 talk (LLMs as utilities/fabs/operating systems).

assertions.claim: Founded Eureka Labs, 'a new kind of school that is AI native': 'The teacher still designs the course materials, but they are supported, leveraged and scaled with an AI Teaching Assistant.'
assumptions: LLMs are reliable enough to tutor at scale
Expert-designed courses plus AI TAs beat either alone
assertions.predictedOutcome: An AI-native education product (starting with LLM101n) reaches learners at scale.
assertions.contextAtTime: Mid-2024: Khanmigo and other AI tutors were emerging. Karpathy had just left OpenAI.
assertions.outcome: Karpathy released educational open-source projects. By May 2026 he joined Anthropic's pretraining team. Eureka Labs' status (paused or continuing) is unclear in coverage.
assertions.verdictRationale: No evidence of scaled product outcomes either way, and the founder's move to Anthropic leaves the venture's trajectory uncertain.
assertions.evolution: Left to join Anthropic (May 2026). One report says he plans to resume education work later.

assertions.claim: There's a new kind of coding, 'vibe coding', where you 'fully give in to the vibes, embrace exponentials, and forget that the code even exists', which works for throwaway projects with LLM coding tools.
assumptions: Coding models are good enough to produce working small apps without line-by-line review
assertions.predictedOutcome: Non-review, prompt-driven app creation becomes a viable mode for low-stakes software.
assertions.contextAtTime: Cursor Composer, Claude 3.5/3.7 Sonnet-era tools. Agentic coding just emerging.
assertions.outcome: The term went mainstream, and an industry of 'vibe coding' app builders grew in 2025–26. Security and quality concerns accompanied it. Karpathy later distinguished it from disciplined 'agentic engineering'.
assertions.verdictRationale: A descriptive claim about an emerging practice that proved widely adopted. He scoped it to throwaway projects, a caveat often lost in later hype.
assertions.evolution: By Dec 2025–Jan 2026 he emphasized serious agentic workflows and said he felt 'behind' as a programmer.

assertions.claim: "When I see things like oh 2025 is the year of agents I get very concerned and I kind of feel like you know this is the decade of agents". Builders should make partial-autonomy products (an 'autonomy slider', humans verifying) rather than fully autonomous agents.
assumptions: Reliability ('march of nines') takes years per step, as in self-driving
LLMs remain fallible and need human verification
assertions.predictedOutcome: Fully autonomous, reliable general agents take roughly a decade (≈2025–2035). Near-term value comes from human-in-the-loop tools.
assertions.contextAtTime: Industry marketing in 2025 billed it 'the year of agents'. Agent benchmarks were improving, but enterprise deployments were brittle.
assertions.outcome: By Oct 2026 coding agents are widely used with human oversight. Fully autonomous general-purpose agents replacing workers are not established. The horizon has not passed.
assertions.verdictRationale: The 10-year horizon runs to ~2035. The partial-autonomy advice matches how coding agents were actually adopted, but full autonomy is untested.
assertions.evolution: Repeated on Dwarkesh (Oct 2025). Softened for coding specifically in Jan 2026.

assertions.claim: AGI and mature agents are still about a decade away. Current agents 'just don't work' as employees: they lack sufficient intelligence, multimodality, computer use and continual learning. RL is 'terrible' (but everything else is worse). AI will likely blend into the existing ~2% GDP growth trend rather than produce a discontinuity.
assumptions: Continual learning and other cognitive gaps need years of research
Diffusion of automation is gradual as with past technologies
assertions.predictedOutcome: No AGI or employee-replacing agents before ~2035, and no visible break in GDP growth trend.
assertions.contextAtTime: Oct 2025: GPT-5 and Claude 4.x-era models. Lab leaders (Amodei, Altman) talked of powerful AI by 2026–2027. Karpathy explicitly called the estimate intuition.
assertions.outcome: Within three months he reported coding agents had crossed a coherence threshold (Jan 2026). By Oct 2026 AGI is not established and no macro GDP discontinuity is documented. The horizon has not passed.
assertions.verdictRationale: The deadline is ~2035. His January 2026 update concerns coding agents, not the broader agent/AGI claim, so it is an evolution, not a falsification.
assertions.evolution: Jan 2026: 'threshold of coherence... phase shift in software engineering' for coding agents. May 2026: joined Anthropic to use Claude to accelerate pretraining, a sign he now treats AI-accelerated research as near-term.

assertions.claim: Camera-only vision with neural networks and fleet data is the scalable path to self-driving. Lidar-based approaches require pre-mapping, and maintaining HD maps is unscalable. In 2025 he cautioned that self-driving is not 'solved' and reliability is a long 'march of nines'.
assumptions: Neural nets can extract depth/velocity from cameras as well as lidar
Fleet data scale compensates for sensor limits
assertions.predictedOutcome: A vision-only stack eventually achieves driverless operation at scale more cheaply than lidar+HD-map stacks. Reliability takes many years.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2019–2021: Waymo (lidar + HD maps) ran limited driverless service. Tesla dropped radar in 2021. Musk was promising FSD 'this year' annually.
assertions.outcome: By late 2025 Tesla ran limited robotaxi service (from June 2025) while lidar-based Waymo scaled paid driverless service. Karpathy said in Oct 2025 'We still haven't declared success' but expects success. Tesla's unsupervised status in 2026 was not verified this session.
assertions.verdictRationale: Vision-only has not yet been shown to work at scale unsupervised, nor been shown impossible. His 2025 caution about the 'march of nines' is consistent with observed slow progress. No dated timeline was found to score.
assertions.evolution: Shift in emphasis from vision-only optimism (2019–21) to stressing long reliability tails (2025). No explicit reversal on vision-only.

assertions.claim: Released 'autoresearch' (an agent autonomously edits training code, runs short experiments and keeps improvements), then joined Anthropic (May 2026) to lead a group using Claude to accelerate large-scale pretraining research.
assumptions: AI agents can productively automate parts of ML research given clear metrics
assertions.predictedOutcome: AI agents materially accelerate frontier model training research.
assertions.contextAtTime: Early 2026: coding agents had just become reliable enough for long autonomous loops. Labs publicly targeted automated AI researchers.
assertions.outcome: autoresearch saw rapid adoption (tens of thousands of GitHub stars) and reported small gains on narrow metrics (e.g., 'time to GPT-2' 2.02h to 1.80h). Impact on frontier pretraining is not yet public.
assertions.verdictRationale: Early demonstrations exist only on narrow, single-metric tasks. Frontier-scale acceleration is undocumented as of Oct 2026.
assertions.evolution: Represents an update from his Oct 2025 skepticism about agent capability.

assertions.claim: Large-scale, diverse labeled data (ImageNet) rather than better hand-designed models is the key to visual recognition. In her 2017 words, 'Data will redefine how we think about models.'
assumptions: Learning algorithms can exploit orders of magnitude more data
Crowdsourced labeling at scale is feasible and accurate enough
assertions.predictedOutcome: Models trained on large datasets dramatically outperform prior methods on recognition.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2006–2009: computer vision focused on features and models with small datasets (e.g., Caltech-101, PASCAL VOC). The co-author called the data-first idea 'a very bold hypothesis'.
assertions.outcome: AlexNet's ILSVRC 2012 win on ImageNet launched the deep-learning era. Data scale became central to all subsequent foundation-model scaling.
assertions.verdictRationale: The data-centric bet was contrarian in 2009 and was decisively vindicated by 2012 and by every subsequent scaling wave.
assertions.evolution: Later extended the data/grounding argument to 3D spatial data and world models (2024–25).

assertions.claim: AI should be 'human-centered': reflect more of the depth of human intelligence, enhance rather than replace humans, and be guided at each step by concern for its human impact. 'there is nothing "artificial" about this technology'.
assumptions: Universities, industry and government coordinate
Designers can choose augmentation over replacement
assertions.predictedOutcome: An interdisciplinary, augmentation-focused AI agenda takes hold in research and policy.
assertions.contextAtTime: March 2018, while she was Google Cloud chief scientist amid the Project Maven controversy. Ethics-in-AI discourse was growing.
assertions.outcome: Stanford HAI (2019) institutionalized the framing and 'human-centered AI' became common policy vocabulary. Industry deployment in 2025–26 increasingly targets labor substitution (agents), so the augmentation goal is contested.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is an aspiration, not a forecast. Its institutional uptake is clear, but whether AI is developed as augmentation rather than replacement remains open.
assertions.evolution: Consistent through 2025. Reapplied to spatial intelligence ('AI to augment human creativity and robotics').

assertions.claim: Co-founded Stanford HAI to advance human-centered AI research, education and policy.
assumptions: Academic institutions can shape AI policy and norms
assertions.predictedOutcome: HAI becomes an influential policy and research hub.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2019: AI ethics institutes proliferating. Industry dominance of AI research was growing.
assertions.outcome: HAI produced the widely cited AI Index and led the NAIRR advocacy coalition. Li served on the federal NAIRR Task Force.
assertions.verdictRationale: The implied belief, that an academic center could materially shape US AI policy, is supported by HAI's role in NAIRR and in indicators like the AI Index.
assertions.evolution: Li moved her primary focus to World Labs from 2024 while remaining HAI co-director.

assertions.claim: The US government should create a National AI Research Resource giving academic and public-sector researchers access to compute and government datasets, because they are falling behind industry.
assumptions: Compute access is the binding constraint for academic AI
A government-funded resource can be built at meaningful scale
assertions.predictedOutcome: Without public compute, academia's share of frontier AI research shrinks. With NAIRR, it can remain competitive.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2019: training costs rising quickly. GPT-2 era. Academia already struggling to train frontier models.
assertions.outcome: The NAIRR Task Force was created (2021) and NSF launched a NAIRR Pilot in January 2024. Frontier model development became overwhelmingly industrial. Full-scale NAIRR funding by Oct 2026 was not verified.
assertions.verdictRationale: Her diagnosis that academia would be priced out of frontier AI proved correct. The remedy was adopted only at pilot scale, far below industry compute.
assertions.evolution: Repeated in later testimony and in the SB 1047 op-ed (concern for public sector/academia).

assertions.claim: "If passed into law, SB-1047 will harm our budding AI ecosystem, especially the parts of it that are already at a disadvantage to today's tech giants: the public sector, academia, and 'little tech.'"
assumptions: Developer liability and kill-switch provisions chill open-source release
Developers cannot foresee all downstream uses
assertions.predictedOutcome: If enacted, SB 1047 would reduce open-model release and academic/startup innovation.
assertions.contextAtTime: Aug 2024: SB 1047 passing the California legislature. Bengio and Hinton supported it. a16z (World Labs' lead investor) led opposition.
assertions.outcome: Gov. Newsom vetoed SB 1047 in late Sept 2024. California later enacted the transparency-focused SB 53 (2025), informed by a working group Li co-led.
assertions.verdictRationale: The condition (enactment) never occurred, so the counterfactual harm cannot be tested.
assertions.evolution: Evolved toward endorsing evidence-based transparency requirements via the 2025 California frontier-AI policy report she co-led (recalled; not re-verified).

assertions.claim: Co-founded World Labs ($230M) to build 'large world models' with spatial intelligence that perceive, generate and interact with 3D worlds. The company targeted a first product in 2025.
assumptions: 3D/spatial generation is a distinct capability not delivered by LLM scaling
Markets exist in creative tools, gaming, simulation and robotics
assertions.predictedOutcome: World Labs ships a commercial world-model product in 2025, and spatial intelligence becomes a major frontier.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2024: Sora previews. LLM scaling dominant. 'World models' a niche topic outside robotics/LeCun's JEPA work.
assertions.outcome: Marble launched commercially on 12 Nov 2025. World Labs raised $1B (Feb 2026; Autodesk $200M) and AMD agreed on ~29 Sept 2026 to acquire it for ~$8.2B in stock, with Li to become AMD chief scientist. Product revenue scale is undisclosed.
assertions.verdictRationale: The first product shipped in 2025 as planned, and world models became a heavily funded frontier. The strategic bet won strong market validation, though valuation is not proof of realized economic returns.
assertions.evolution: Articulated more fully in 'From Words to Worlds' (Nov 2025). Pivoted to hardware-company ownership with the AMD deal (Sept 2026).

assertions.claim: Spatial intelligence is AI's next frontier. Language models lack grounding in space, motion and physical consequence (multimodal models rarely beat chance at estimating distance, orientation and size). True world models must be able to generate consistent 3D worlds (her other two required capabilities, recalled as multimodal and interactive, were not confirmed this session).
assumptions: Spatial reasoning won't emerge sufficiently from scaling text/video models
New 3D data and architectures are needed
assertions.predictedOutcome: World models become the next major capability wave, enabling robotics, simulation and creative tools beyond LLMs.
assertions.contextAtTime: Late 2025: Genie 3, Nvidia Cosmos and others pushing world models. LeCun leaving Meta to pursue world models. LLMs still dominant commercially.
assertions.outcome: Investment in world models rose sharply in 2026 (World Labs $1B round, AMD acquisition). LLM-based systems remain the dominant commercial AI. Whether spatial intelligence is 'the' next frontier is undetermined.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is an open-ended directional claim. Capital flows support salience but do not establish technical primacy.
assertions.evolution: Consistent with her 2024 World Labs thesis and her lifelong vision-first view.

assertions.claim: "I frankly don't even know what AGI means." In Nov 2025 she called AGI more of a marketing term than a rigorous scientific one.
assumptions: Scientific rigor requires operational definitions
assertions.predictedOutcome: No testable prediction. Rejects AGI-timeline framing.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2024–25: lab CEOs (Altman, Amodei, Hassabis) publicly offering AGI timelines.
assertions.outcome: No consensus definition of AGI emerged by Oct 2026. Contractual and benchmark definitions proliferated.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is a definitional opinion and not falsifiable.
assertions.evolution: Hardened from agnosticism (2024) to calling it a marketing term (2025).

assertions.claim: The biggest lesson from 70 years of AI research is that general methods that leverage computation are ultimately the most effective, by a large margin, because computation keeps getting exponentially cheaper. Methods building in human knowledge help short-term but plateau and inhibit progress.
assumptions: Moore's-law-like growth in available computation continues
General learning/search methods scale with compute
assertions.predictedOutcome: Over time, compute-scaled general methods will beat knowledge-engineered approaches across AI domains.
assertions.contextAtTime: March 2019: GPT-2 just released. AlphaZero and deep learning successes in vision/speech. Many researchers still invested in domain-specific inductive biases.
assertions.outcome: 2020–2026 scaling (GPT-3/4, scaling laws, RL-on-LLMs, massive data-center buildouts) broadly confirmed that compute-scaled general methods dominate. The essay became a canonical reference for scaling advocates.
assertions.verdictRationale: Judged on 2019 information, it was a strong directional bet that the subsequent scaling era bore out. Sutton himself argues LLMs' reliance on human data is only a partial application of the lesson.
assertions.evolution: No revision. In 2025 he applied it against LLMs (human-data dependence).

assertions.claim: Search and learning are the two general methods that scale arbitrarily with computation.
assumptions: Both training-time learning and inference-time search convert compute into capability
assertions.predictedOutcome: Both learning (training) and search (inference-time computation) will be major sources of capability gains.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2019: learning-at-scale was ascendant. Inference-time search was mostly associated with game-playing (MCTS).
assertions.outcome: From 2024 inference-time compute (o1/o3 reasoning, test-time search on ARC, parallel sampling) became a second scaling axis alongside training.
assertions.verdictRationale: The 2024–26 rise of test-time/inference scaling matches his pairing of search with learning. The 'search' is chain-of-thought sampling rather than classical tree search.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: The Alberta Plan: AI research should focus on agents that learn continually, online, from a single stream of experience, building and planning with learned world models.
assumptions: Continual-learning algorithms can be made stable and efficient
Experience-based agents generalize better than static pretrained models
assertions.predictedOutcome: Continual, experiential RL agents become the path to general intelligence.
assertions.contextAtTime: Aug 2022: pre-ChatGPT, with large language models scaling via static pretraining.
assertions.outcome: Continual learning was widely cited by 2025–26 (including by Karpathy) as a key missing capability of LLM agents. Frontier systems still rely on static pretraining plus RL post-training.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is a long-run research agenda. Its diagnosis (lack of continual learning) gained mainstream recognition, but the approach is unproven at frontier scale.
assertions.evolution: Continued via Keen Technologies and the Era of Experience paper (2025).

assertions.claim: Succession to AI (or AI-augmented beings) is inevitable and should be welcomed as the next step in the evolution of intelligence rather than resisted out of fear.
assumptions: Superhuman AI will be built
Value lies in intelligence/complexity rather than specifically human control
assertions.predictedOutcome: Humans will eventually be succeeded by AI as the dominant intelligence.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2023: Hinton and Bengio raising existential-risk alarms. CAIS extinction-risk statement (May 2023). Pause letter (Mar 2023).
assertions.outcome: No succession has occurred. The debate continues, with Sutton among the most prominent researchers rejecting the doom framing.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is a long-horizon normative and predictive claim and cannot be evaluated yet.
assertions.evolution: No revision found. Venue and date recalled, not verified.

assertions.claim: Joined John Carmack's Keen Technologies to pursue AGI through RL-based agents with a small team, outside the LLM mainstream.
assumptions: AGI does not require frontier-scale LLM compute
Experience-driven RL is the right path
assertions.predictedOutcome: A small RL-focused lab makes significant progress toward general agents.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2023: capital concentrating in LLM labs. Carmack publicly betting on non-LLM paths.
assertions.outcome: No breakthrough results from Keen Technologies were documented in this session's research.
assertions.verdictRationale: No public results allow evaluation.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: LLMs are a dead end for reaching real intelligence. They imitate what people say rather than learn from experience, have no goal or ground truth, and are not true world models. Systems that learn from experience will supersede them, as the Bitter Lesson implies.
assumptions: Human-data imitation caps capability
Experience-based RL can scale beyond it
assertions.predictedOutcome: The dominant paradigm will shift from LLM pretraining to agents learning from experience.
assertions.contextAtTime: Sept 2025: reasoning models trained with RL on verifiable rewards were rising (a partial move toward his view). LLM capex was at record levels.
assertions.outcome: As of Oct 2026 LLM-based systems remain dominant and continue improving. RL post-training and agentic training environments became increasingly central, blending imitation with experience. No paradigm replacement has occurred.
assertions.verdictRationale: No deadline was given. Disagreement from LLM proponents does not falsify it, and LLM progress through 2026 does not confirm it either.
assertions.evolution: Consistent with the Alberta Plan (2022) and Era of Experience (2025). Karpathy published a partial rebuttal ('Animals vs Ghosts').

assertions.claim: Deep neural networks (policy and value nets) combined with Monte Carlo tree search and RL from self-play can master Go at professional level, a feat previously thought to be a decade away.
assumptions: Learned evaluation can replace hand-crafted heuristics in huge search spaces
assertions.predictedOutcome: AlphaGo defeats top human professionals.
assertions.contextAtTime: Before 2016 the best Go programs played at strong amateur level. Many experts expected professional-level Go AI to be ~10 years away.
assertions.outcome: AlphaGo beat Lee Sedol 4–1 in March 2016.
assertions.verdictRationale: The demonstrated method decisively beat the world-class professional, years ahead of expert expectations.
assertions.evolution: Generalized to AlphaGo Zero/AlphaZero (2017) and MuZero (2019).

assertions.claim: An algorithm learning tabula rasa from self-play, without human data or guidance, can exceed systems trained on human expert knowledge (AlphaGo Zero).
assumptions: A perfect simulator/verifier (game rules) provides unlimited grounded reward
assertions.predictedOutcome: Self-generated experience can surpass human data where reward is well-defined.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2017: deep learning broadly relied on human-labeled data. AlphaGo had used human games.
assertions.outcome: Demonstrated in Go, then chess/shogi (AlphaZero). By 2024–26 RL on verifiable rewards (math, code) became a core LLM training technique, though language models still start from human-data pretraining.
assertions.verdictRationale: Correct within domains with verifiable rewards, and the idea later transferred to reasoning-model training. Human data remains foundational outside such domains.
assertions.evolution: Generalized into the 'Era of Experience' thesis (2025).

assertions.claim: A single general RL algorithm (AlphaZero), given only the rules, can reach superhuman performance across multiple games (chess, shogi, Go).
assumptions: Generality across domains with known rules and simulators
assertions.predictedOutcome: AlphaZero beats the strongest specialized engines (Stockfish, Elmo) and AlphaGo Zero.
assertions.contextAtTime: Top chess engines relied on decades of hand-tuned evaluation functions.
assertions.outcome: Results were published in Science (Dec 2018). Neural-network evaluation was later adopted by mainstream engines (e.g., Stockfish NNUE).
assertions.verdictRationale: Demonstrated, peer-reviewed result that reshaped computer chess.
assertions.evolution: Extended to unknown-model settings via MuZero.

assertions.claim: 'Reward is enough': maximizing reward in a rich environment is sufficient to drive behaviour exhibiting most if not all attributes of intelligence (knowledge, perception, language, social intelligence, generalization).
assumptions: Sufficiently rich environments and capable RL agents exist
Sample efficiency can be overcome
assertions.predictedOutcome: General intelligence can emerge from reward maximization alone.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2021: GPT-3 showed that self-supervised pretraining on human data, not RL, drove the most general behaviour seen. Critics called the hypothesis unfalsifiable.
assertions.outcome: Frontier general capabilities came primarily from self-supervised pretraining, with RL increasingly decisive for reasoning and agentic behaviour (2024–26). No system has shown general intelligence from reward alone.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is a broad sufficiency hypothesis with no horizon. The RL post-training trend is consistent with it, but the dominant role of pretraining in 2020–26 is a counterpoint, not a refutation.
assertions.evolution: Reaffirmed in 'Era of Experience' (2025).

assertions.claim: RL with formal verification (AlphaProof, training on self-generated/auto-formalized problems in Lean), together with AlphaGeometry 2, reaches IMO silver-medal standard: a path to advanced mathematical reasoning.
assumptions: Formal verifiers provide grounded reward for math
Self-play-style RL transfers from games to proofs
assertions.predictedOutcome: Formal-RL systems reach top human olympiad performance and beyond.
assertions.contextAtTime: July 2024: LLMs performed poorly on olympiad proofs, before OpenAI o1.
assertions.outcome: AlphaProof/AlphaGeometry 2 scored 28/42 (silver standard) at IMO 2024, with manual formalization and long compute times. At IMO 2025 a natural-language Gemini Deep Think (and an OpenAI model) reached gold standard within time limits, without formal Lean.
assertions.verdictRationale: The 2024 result was real and landmark, and RL proved central. But the next jump came from RL-trained natural-language LLMs rather than the formal-RL route AlphaProof embodied.
assertions.evolution: AlphaProof published in Nature (late 2025, recalled). Silver's framing shifted to experience-driven agents generally.

assertions.claim: Welcome to the Era of Experience (with Sutton): the era of human data is reaching its limits. Agents will increasingly learn from their own long-running streams of experience with grounded actions and rewards, and experiential data will come to eclipse human data.
assumptions: High-quality human data is approaching exhaustion
Environments with grounded rewards can be built at scale
assertions.predictedOutcome: The dominant source of capability gains shifts from human-data pretraining to experiential RL.
assertions.contextAtTime: Apr 2025: o1/o3 and DeepSeek-R1 had shown RL on verifiable rewards. Concerns about 'peak data' were widespread (Sutskever, Dec 2024).
assertions.outcome: Through 2026 labs scaled RL environments and agentic training substantially, but pretraining on human data remains foundational. No clear shift to experience-dominant training is documented.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is directional and open-ended. Trends are consistent with it but have not yet borne it out.
assertions.evolution: Reportedly acted on by founding a startup in 2026 (low-confidence recall).

assertions.claim: Reportedly left Google DeepMind to found Ineffable Intelligence, a startup pursuing experience-driven RL toward superintelligence.
assumptions: Experience-driven RL warrants a dedicated lab outside big tech
assertions.predictedOutcome: A new lab advances the Era-of-Experience agenda.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2026: wave of researcher-founded labs (e.g., Sutskever's SSI, Murati's Thinking Machines, LeCun's world-model venture).
assertions.outcome: Not verified this session.
assertions.verdictRationale: Unverified recall and no public results.
assertions.evolution: n/a

assertions.claim: Released Keras, a minimalist high-level deep-learning API, to make deep learning accessible to every developer.
assumptions: Developer accessibility is the bottleneck to deep-learning adoption
assertions.predictedOutcome: Broad developer adoption of deep learning via a simple API.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2015: Theano/Caffe/Torch required expertise. TensorFlow was not yet released (Nov 2015).
assertions.outcome: Keras became TensorFlow's official high-level API and one of the most-used deep-learning frameworks. Keras 3 (2023) supports JAX/PyTorch/TensorFlow. PyTorch later dominated research.
assertions.verdictRationale: Massive adoption validated the accessibility thesis, though PyTorch overtook TF/Keras in research.
assertions.evolution: No revision.

assertions.claim: An 'intelligence explosion' is impossible. Intelligence is situational and bounded by environment, body and culture, and recursively self-improving systems hit bottlenecks, so progress will be roughly linear rather than explosive.
assumptions: Bottlenecks (data, experiment time, environment) scale with capability
assertions.predictedOutcome: No runaway recursive self-improvement.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2017: Bostrom-style takeoff arguments prominent in safety circles.
assertions.outcome: As of Oct 2026 no intelligence explosion has occurred. AI-assisted AI research has emerged (e.g., Karpathy's autoresearch, Anthropic using Claude to accelerate pretraining), so the question is newly live.
assertions.verdictRationale: This is an impossibility claim with no horizon. The absence of an explosion so far is weak evidence, and the claim cannot be confirmed.
assertions.evolution: No revision found.

assertions.claim: Intelligence is skill-acquisition efficiency, not skill at specific tasks. Benchmarks of task skill can be 'bought' with data/priors and so do not measure general intelligence. ARC measures human-like fluid intelligence and resists approaches without broad generalization.
assumptions: ARC tasks are novel enough that memorization/scale won't solve them
assertions.predictedOutcome: ARC remains unsolved by systems lacking efficient generalization, even as conventional benchmarks saturate.
assertions.contextAtTime: 2019: GPT-2. Benchmarks such as GLUE were being saturated rapidly.
assertions.outcome: ARC-AGI-1 resisted LLM scaling from 2019 to mid-2024 (GPT-4-class models scored low). It fell to o3's test-time reasoning in Dec 2024. ARC became a standard frontier-lab benchmark.
assertions.verdictRationale: ARC outlasted many benchmarks through five years of scaling, as he argued. It fell only to systems with explicit test-time adaptation, consistent with his definition.
assertions.evolution: Created ARC-AGI-2 (2025) and ARC-AGI-3 to maintain the human-AI gap measurement.

assertions.claim: LLMs as trained mostly memorize and retrieve patterns/programs and cannot adapt to genuine novelty. Scaling them will not solve ARC or lead to AGI, and a $1M ARC Prize would show it.
assumptions: Pretraining scale doesn't produce test-time adaptation
ARC private set is unmemorizable
assertions.predictedOutcome: Pure LLM scaling will not achieve high ARC-AGI scores.
assertions.contextAtTime: June 2024: GPT-4o-class models scored roughly 5–10% on ARC-AGI-1. o1 had not been announced.
assertions.outcome: In Dec 2024 o3, an LLM with RL-trained chain-of-thought and heavy test-time compute, scored 75.7% (within budget) and 87.5% (high compute) on ARC-AGI-1. Chollet attributed this to test-time program search, not pretraining scale.
assertions.verdictRationale: He was right that pretraining scale alone did not crack ARC. But LLM-based systems did, within six months, via reasoning/test-time compute, which undercuts the stronger 'LLMs won't get there' reading.
assertions.evolution: Updated after o3 (Dec 2024), calling it a genuine breakthrough.

assertions.claim: OpenAI set back progress toward AGI by roughly 5–10 years, by closing frontier research publication and pulling the field's attention and resources onto LLMs.
assumptions: AGI requires approaches other than LLMs
Open publication drives progress
assertions.predictedOutcome: Non-testable counterfactual about research trajectory.
assertions.contextAtTime: Mid-2024: frontier labs had stopped publishing details. LLM capex surging.
assertions.outcome: Counterfactual. Reasoning models arrived within months, which some read as rapid progress via the LLM path.
assertions.verdictRationale: A counterfactual opinion that cannot be falsified.
assertions.evolution: Tone softened toward LLM-based reasoning after o3, but no explicit retraction found.

assertions.claim: o3's ARC-AGI-1 score is a genuine breakthrough, a step-function increase in test-time adaptation, but passing ARC-AGI does not equal AGI and o3 is not AGI. ARC-AGI-2 will still challenge o3, potentially reducing its score to under 30% even at high compute, while smart humans score far higher.
assumptions: ARC-AGI-2 tasks require compositional generalization beyond o3
assertions.predictedOutcome: o3 scores under 30% on ARC-AGI-2.
assertions.contextAtTime: Dec 2024: o3 just announced. ARC-AGI-2 in development.
assertions.outcome: At ARC-AGI-2's launch (Mar 2025) frontier reasoning models including o3 scored in the low single digits. Later frontier systems with refinement reportedly reached roughly 45–55% by late 2025 (low-confidence recall).
assertions.verdictRationale: The specific forecast about o3 on ARC-AGI-2 held by a wide margin. The 'not AGI' judgment is consistent with persistent gaps.
assertions.evolution: This was itself an update toward LLM-based reasoning.

assertions.claim: Co-founded Ndea (with Mike Knoop) to build AGI via deep-learning-guided program synthesis, arguing it is the missing ingredient for efficient test-time adaptation.
assumptions: Program synthesis + DL yields more efficient generalization than LLM scaling
assertions.predictedOutcome: A program-synthesis lab produces systems with superior generalization efficiency.
assertions.contextAtTime: Jan 2025: reasoning models ascendant. Chollet had left Google (Nov 2024).
assertions.outcome: No major Ndea results were verified this session.
assertions.verdictRationale: No public results allow evaluation.
assertions.evolution: n/a

assertions.claim: ARC-AGI-2 (and the interactive ARC-AGI-3) will continue to expose a large gap between AI and human fluid intelligence: tasks easy for humans remain hard for AI.
assumptions: New task distributions defeat current test-time methods
assertions.predictedOutcome: Frontier AI scores on ARC-AGI-2/3 remain well below human performance for a sustained period.
assertions.contextAtTime: Mar 2025: o3 near zero on ARC-AGI-2. Lab leaders forecasting rapid AGI.
assertions.outcome: Frontier scores on ARC-AGI-2 rose substantially in late 2025 (reported ~45–55% for top systems, low-confidence recall). The ARC Prize 2025 grand prize under compute limits went unclaimed. ARC-AGI-3 and July–Oct 2026 results could not be verified.
assertions.verdictRationale: The gap persisted under efficiency constraints but narrowed quickly for unconstrained frontier systems. The verdict is tentative given unverified 2026 data.
assertions.evolution: Chollet moved to interactive ARC-AGI-3 to keep the benchmark ahead of systems.

relations.note: In Oct 2025 he said agents 'just don't work' and called this the decade of agents. In Jan 2026 he said coding agents crossed a 'threshold of coherence' in Dec 2025 and moved to ~80% agent coding.
At Tesla Autonomy Day Karpathy argued vision is sufficient without lidar, alongside Musk's 'fool's errand' remark. He reiterated it at CVPR 2021.

Around Tesla's robotaxi launch Karpathy warned against believing self-driving is 'solved', and later described a long 'march of nines'. Electrek reads this as contradicting Musk, though Karpathy did not name Tesla.

Responding to Sutton's Dwarkesh interview, Karpathy argued LLMs are 'ghosts' bootstrapped from human data rather than 'animals' learning from experience. He accepted part of the critique but defended pretraining as a practical path.
Founded AI-native education company.
Coined the term 'vibe coding'.
Li's Fortune op-ed opposed California SB 1047. Bengio published a direct Fortune rebuttal nine days later supporting the bill.
Andreessen Horowitz (firm, not a personal investment) co-led World Labs' $230M launch financing. a16z also led opposition to SB 1047, which Li also opposed.
Co-founded and led World Labs. AMD agreed to acquire it in Sept 2026.

Hinton's group (Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton) used Li's ImageNet/ILSVRC to demonstrate AlexNet, launching the deep-learning era. The dependency is on ImageNet as infrastructure, not a stated intellectual debt.

Argued LLMs are a dead end because they imitate human data rather than learn from experience. He reads the Bitter Lesson as ultimately favoring experiential learners over LLMs, unlike scaling advocates who cite it in favor of LLMs.
Both argue LLMs lack grounded world models and will not by themselves yield human-level intelligence. Their preferred remedies differ (RL from experience vs. self-supervised world models/JEPA).
Sutton framed succession to AI as inevitable and positive, opposing the existential-risk alarm raised by Hinton (and Bengio) in 2023.
Co-authored 'Reward is enough' (2021) and 'Welcome to the Era of Experience' (2025).
Silver did his PhD at the University of Alberta in Sutton's RL group (recalled; not re-verified).
Lead researcher on AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero at DeepMind (under Demis Hassabis).
Said OpenAI set back AGI progress by roughly 5–10 years by closing research and focusing the field on LLMs.
After o3's ARC-AGI-1 score, Chollet called it a genuine breakthrough in test-time adaptation (while maintaining it was not AGI), updating from his view that LLMs could not adapt to novelty.

Both argue LLMs rely on memorization/pattern-matching and lack robust generalization, and both favor hybrid/symbolic-like components (program synthesis for Chollet). Chollet is more open to deep learning as a component.
Created ARC (2019), co-founded the ARC Prize (2024), and released ARC-AGI-2 (2025) and ARC-AGI-3.
Co-founded program-synthesis AGI lab with Mike Knoop.
Argued task-skill benchmarks can be 'bought' with data and scale, so scaling does not measure or produce general intelligence. This set him against the scaling camp (e.g., Sutskever, Altman, Amodei).

Joined Anthropic's pretraining team (under Nick Joseph) to use Claude to accelerate pretraining research. This is an employment move, recorded as alignment with Anthropic's AI-accelerated-research approach.
